 JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.12,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the insurer and owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-X-0680 alleging that on 13.08.2020 at about 4.15 p.m.
when he was walking from APMC Market towards home at Kolar town on the service road of Bengaluru Chennai, NH-75, rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-X-0680, rode the same negligently dashed the same to the petitioner , thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Immediately after the accident, petitioner has been shifted to Narendra hospital, Kolar , wherein taken treatment by spending Rs.3,00,000/-.

sentences.text: 3. As on the date of accident petitioner being aged 19 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/p p.m. by working at SN Mandi, APMC Market Kolar.
Regarding the accident Kolar Traffic police registered a case in crime No.32/2020 against the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-X-0680 for the offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC .

4. In response to the notice, respondents appeared through their respective Advocates, on 08.06.2022 respondent No.1, on 02.01.2021, respondent No.2 owner of the motorcycle filed written statements denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of the accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

In the written statement respondent No.1 insurance company specifically denied the involvement of the motorcycle in the accident and further asserted that the person who rode the motorcycle during the alleged accident had no licence to ride the motorcycle and therefore, another person has been inserted as rider of the motorcycle who had licence to ride the motorcycle with gear.

5. On the basis of the pleadings on 18.09.2021, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-X-0680 by its rider accident has occurred on 13.08.2020 to the petitioner who was proceeding as pedestrian and he sustained injuries in the accident ?
2. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the accident has occurred on account of negligent act of petitioner himself?

6. On 30.10.2021, 28.12.2021,12.10.2022, petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 12 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.12.
On 09.12.2022 petitioner produced the evidence of Dr.Narendra as PW2 and produced 3 documents at Ex.P.13 to P.15.

On 27,03,2023 , 19.04.2023, 02.06.2023, 19.07.2023 respondent No.1 insurance company produced the evidence of Officer and Investigation Authority as RW1 and 2 and produced 5 documents which includes AVR CD and pendrive at Ex.R.1 to R.6.

On 05.03.2024,27.03.2024, respondent No.2 owner of the motorcycle produced the evidence of rider of the motorcycle as RW3.
7.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.

8. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 ...
In the affirmative  Issue No.2 ...
In the Negative  Issue No.3 ...

Petitioner is entitled to Rs.7,56,391/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.4 ...

As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 9. Issues No.1 and 2 :- In the claim petition and in the evidence affidavit petitioner/PW1 stated that on 13.08.2020 at about 4.15 p.m. when walking from APMC Market towards home at Kolar on the service road of Bengaluru Chennai, NH-75, rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-X-0680, rode the same negligently dashed the same to the petitioner , thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
10. In the written statement respondents No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
In the written statement , respondent No.1 insurance company specifically asserted that motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-X-0680 never caused accident.

Respondent No.1 further asserted that during alleged accident, the person who rode the motorcycle, respondent No.2 had no licence to ride the vehicle, therefore, B.C.Ananthapadmanabha has been inserted/implicated as rider of the motorcycle.

11. In the cross-examination , PW1 petitioner stated that there was delay of 15 days in filing the complaint from the date of the accident and Shaif Khan filed the complaint about the accident to the police.
PW1 admitted that in the service road which is measuring 15 feet accident taken place.

PW1 admitted the existence of footpath beside the service road and after the accident he was shifted to Arbaz Khan vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56997347/
3 Narendra hospital .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW1 stated that in the hospital informed the mode of accident .
PW1 stated that rider of the motorcycle which involved in the accident did not accompany him to the hospital.
PW1 denied the suggestion that as per the sketch marked at Ex.P.5 accident taken place in the middle of the service road and explained that the accident taken place on the side of the divider.
PW1 stated that the sketch prepared by the police is not correct and admitted that the accident should not have been happened if he walked on the footpath situated on the service road.
PW1 denied the suggestion that due to his negligence accident taken place, therefore, belatedly filed the complaint.
12. In the evidence PW2 Dr.Narendra stated nothing about the reason and mode of accident.

13. In the evidence RW1 officer of the insurance company stated that investigator of the respondent No.1 company filed report along with AVR CD and pendrive stating that chargesheeted person was not riding the motorcycle at the time of accident respondent No.2 insured himself was riding the motorcycle without having licence to ride the motorcycle, thereby contravened terms and conditions of the policy.

14. In the evidence RW1 produced copy of the policy along with FSL report along with certificate as required under Section 65B of Evidence Act, AVR CD and pendrive at Ex.R.2 to R.5.
15.
In the cross-examination RW1 stated that the police by collusion filed chargesheet against Ananthapadmanabha, the rider of the motorcycle .
RW1 stated that Hemanth, Proprietor of Maruthi Enterprises conducted investigation and submitted report.

RW1 denied the suggestion that there is no connection between the parties who are in Ex.R.4 - C.D.
16.

In the evidence RW2 Hemanth J.B., S/o. Balakrishna J.H. the alleged investigator of the respondent No.1 insurance company stated about the investigation was conducted by him and produced investigation report at Ex.R.6.

In the cross-examination, RW2 submitted that he never witnessed the accident and denied the suggestion that he has taken the video of some other person by creating him as the person who caused the accident and created the investigation report.
RW2 admitted that police have recorded the statement of Ananthapadmanabha who caused accident.

17. In the evidence affidavit RW3 B.C.Ananthapadmanabha , the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-X-0680 stated about reason and mode of accident, however stated that the petitioner suddenly came, dashed to the running motorcycle and accident taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner.

RW3 stated that immediately after the accident himself and respondent No.2 shifted the injured to the nearest Orthopaedic hospital , thereby get provided treatment and respondent No.2 beared initial hospital charges worth Rs.50,000/-.
In the cross-examination RW3 stated that the road on which motorcycle was running was Bengaluru- Chennai NH-75.
RW3 admitted non-production of receipt to confirm that he has paid Rs.50,000/- towards hospital charges.
In the cross-examination made on behalf of respondent No.1, RW3 submitted that he has purchased TVS Jupiter scooter from showroom since last 19 years, having licence to drive his scooter.
18. Ex.P.1 and 2 are the copies of FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.32/20 registered on 28.08.2020 by Kolar traffic police regarding the accident taken place on 13.08.2020 at 4.15 p.m.

sentences.text: Ex.P.3 copy of spot mahazar recorded on 28.8.2020, Ex.P.4 the copy of the vehicle seizure mahazar recorded on 29.08.2020, Ex.P.5 copy of sketch place of accident in which it is noted that on East West service road the accident taken place.

Ex.P.6 copy of the Motor Vehicle Report dated 29.08.2020, Ex.P.7 is the copy of wound certificate ,
Ex.P.8 copy of chargesheet filed by Kolar traffic police in crime NO.32/20 against RW3 Ananthapadmanabha B.C. , rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-X-0680 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,338 of IPC regarding accident taken place on 13.08.2020 at 4.15 p.m. resulting in injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.9 discharge summary , history of the injuries are noted as RTA on 13.08.2020 at 4.30p.m. near Bypass Tractor Showroom, patient was crossing road hit by two wheeler.
In the pendrive the discussion between Investigating Officer, and two persons are recorded.

19. The records shows that the service of notice of the petition on respondent No.1 was reported to this authority on 24.11.2020, however, after lapse of approximately more than one year 6 months on 08.06.22 respondent No.1 insurance company filed written statement.

If the respondent No.1 insurance company had sufficient reasons to believe that petitioner , police, respondent No.2, RW3 by colluding with each other get fabricated documents and filed chargesheet noting RW3 B.C.Aananthapadmanabha as rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-X-0680 during alleged accident, the insurance company ought to have taken proper steps by approaching proper authority by proper method.
In this case, at this stage there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner including evidence of RW3 regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 13.08.2020 at about 4.15 p.m. when petitioner was walking from APMC Market towards home on the service road of Bengaluru Chennai, NH-75, Kolar town, Ananthapadmanabha, RW3 the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-X-0680, rode the motorcycle negligently dashed the same to the petitioner , thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative and issue No.2 in the negative.
20. Issue No.3:

In the evidence, petitioner stated that in the accident he was suffered type I compound fracture with bones of right leg and other injuries, took treatment at Narendra hospital,
Kolar as an inpatient from 13.08.2020 to 27.08.2020 by spending Rs.1,00,000/- .
In the written statement respondents denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
In the cross-examination, petitioner denied the suggestion about non-spending of Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment.
21. The deposition shows that on 30.10.2021 , 28.12.2021 petitioner came to Court hall with the help of 4 leg clutches.
22. In the evidence PW2 Dr.Narendra stated that on 23.08.2020 petitioner came to hospital with the history of R.T.A. and took treatment upto 27.08.2020, on 13.08.2020 underwent surgery.

PW2 stated that on 28.02.2020 on clinical examination noticed permanent physical disability to lower limb at 36.6% and to whole body at 12.2% and required to get removal of implants at the cost of Rs.25,000/-.

In the cross-examination PW2 stated that he has treated the petitioner and denied the Arbaz Khan vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56997347/
5 suggestion that disability assessed earlier to removal of implant is temporary disability.

entities.text: Arbaz Khan vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW2 submitted that in Ex.P.13 there is no mention that petitioner has to get remove of implants.
PW2 stated that as per 2018 guidelines the disability of hip, ankle and knee is at 30% each.
23. In the evidence RW1 to 3 stated nothing about the nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

24. Wound certificate , discharge summary , x-ray, medical bills, case files shows that in the accident petitioner suffered type I compound fracture with bones of right leg and other injuries, took treatment at Narendra hospital , Kolar as an inpatient from 13.08.2020 to 27.08.2020, underwent surgery by spending Rs.59,191/-.
In Ex.P.12 copy of Aadhar card date of birth is noted as 01.01.2002.
In the file there are no documentary evidence regarding occupation and income of the petitioner.

Hence, Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards pain and sufferings Rs.59,191/- is awarded towards treatment , Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards attendant and conveyance charges,
Rs.1,74,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period (Rs.14,500x12),
Rs.80,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness, Rs.3,13,200/- is awarded towards loss of future income due to permanent disability by making the calculation in the following terms:
Age of the petitioner as on the date of 19 years accident

Notional income of the petitioner as on the - Rs.14,500/- date of accident Permanent functional disability suffered by Rs.1,450/- the petitioner 10% Loss of future income due to permanent Rs.3,13,200 disability 1450x12x18 25.
Therefore, I came to the conclusion that petitioner is entitle of Rs.7,56,391/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
26. The copy of the policy marked at Ex.R.2 shows that as on the date of accident motorcycle bearing No.KA- 07-X-0680 had insurance coverage with respondent No.1 insurance company.
The evidence of RW3 shows that as on the date of accident RW3 Ananthapadmanabha against whom police have filed chargesheet had licence to ride motorcycle with get.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the insurer and owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-X-0680 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.7,56,391/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.1, being the Insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-07-X-0680 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
